subject: Dedicated capacity: throughput SLA, pool sizing and packaging options
messages:
From: Aisha Rahman <aisha.rahman@hyperion.ai>
To: Elliot Price <elliot_price@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-05-14T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated pool sizing request and workload profile attached

Hi Elliot,

Thanks for taking this — we're excited to partner. Attached is a workbook that summarizes our traffic profile and model mix. High level:~
- Peak QPS: 1,400 reqs/s (90% text-completion, 10% embedding/rerank)
- Average context: 1,900 tokens (we run multi-turn chat history + knowledge snippets)
- Average output tokens: 120 tokens
- Concurrent requests at peak: ~520 active streams
- 95th percentile latency target: <300ms for short completions, <800ms for long/context-heavy calls

We'd like your recommendation for a committed dedicated GPU pool (steady + burst), what throughput guarantees you can commit to, and pricing bands for 12/24-month reserved commits. Also call out fallback behavior to hosted/shared models if pool saturates and how that affects SLAs.

Timeline: procurement begins week of May 20; ideally have a commercial sketch and SLO language this week.

Attachments: Hyperion_Workload_Profile.xlsx (workload workbook)

Best,
Aisha Rahman
CTO, Hyperion AI

Date: 2028-05-14T11:03:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated pool sizing request and workload profile attached

Aisha — thanks, got the workbook. Quick clarifying questions before we size:
1) Is the 1,900 token context the stable average across requests, or is that a 95th percentile?
2) How many parallel KV/cacheable prefixes do you expect (that affects effective batching)?
3) Any hard requirement for p50 vs p95 on the same SLA? (we usually separate short vs long calls)

Initial read: with the mix and generous context, our back-of-envelope is ~10–14 A100-equivalent GPUs for steady-state, with a 30% burst headroom to handle peak surges. That number assumes 16-bit FP/INT8 quantization on some models — we can tighten with more aggressive quantization or sharding.

Looping Marissa for pricing and packaging. I'll pull Ben in for a quick run at modeling if that sounds right.

— Elliot

Subject: Pricing sketch: committed pool + burst + SLA tiers

Aisha — thanks for the workbook and Elliot's notes. Below is a concise commercial sketch to get the conversation moving. Numbers are example bands; we'll lock final pricing after a short benchmarking run and mutual action plan.

1) Recommended configuration (initial):
- Committed pool: 10 A100-eq GPUs (dedicated) for 12 months
- Burst allowance: up to 30% additional GPU time from Redwood shared capacity (subject to availability)
- Canary window & ramp: 45 days for performance tuning and fallback validation

2) Throughput & SLOs (explainers):
- Steady throughput guarantee: 1,100 reqs/s sustained across the committed pool (measured over 5m rolling windows)
- Burst window: up to 1,430 reqs/s for short intervals (up to 10 minutes) with best-effort latency guarantees
- Latency SLA options (pick one):
  A) Standard SLA (no credit): p50 < 250ms, p95 < 700ms
  B) Premium SLA (credits): p50 < 200ms, p95 < 500ms + 99.9% availability for committed pool

3) Pricing bands (USD / month for committed pool, before discount):
- 10 A100-eq: $185,000/mo (baseline list)
- 12 A100-eq: $220,000/mo (if you prefer extra steady headroom)

4) Discounting & packaging (commercial options):
- 12-month: standard 12% volume discount off list
- 12-month, 90% paid upfront: up to 18% discount + 3 months of extended burst credits
- 24-month: 20% discount with guaranteed pricing floor and capacity reservation priority
- Enterprise bundle (Observability + Optimize): additional $12k/mo add-on or 25% off when purchased with committed pool

5) Fallback policy & model substitution:
- If committed pool is exhausted, requests will be routed to an equivalent Redwood-verified model in hosted capacity.
- For Premium SLA, Redwood will maintain a reserved overflow buffer and automated model-substitution rules; credits apply if p95 exceeds SLA for >15m windows.

6) Next steps:
- Ben: can you run a short token/sec/GPU modeling run and confirm the 10 A100-eq estimate against their workbook?
- Aisha: if acceptable, we can draft a term sheet + SLO language and an initial 45-day MAP for benchmarking.

Attachments: Redwood_Pricing_Sketch.pdf

Thanks — happy to jump on a 30-min call to walk numbers.

— Marissa
Sr. AE, Redwood Inference

Marissa / team — appreciate the clear sketch. A few points from procurement/engineering: 
- The pricing bands are directionally OK but we need a stronger p95 guarantee for short completions. Our external SLAs to customers demand p95 < 400ms for requests under 1k tokens.
- Can you quantify how credits are calculated? We prefer a deterministic credit formula tied to minutes of degraded performance.
- We need explicit rollback and canary clauses: if we pick Premium SLA, what's the emergency fallback if your reserved overflow buffer is insufficient?

Procurement timeline: we need a draft commercial term sheet by May 19 to review with legal. Also sending our redlines next (attachment).

From: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-05-17T13:08:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Pricing sketch: committed pool + burst + SLA tiers — modeling notes

Aisha — I ran a quick token/sec model against the workbook you provided. Key assumptions and outcomes below.

Assumptions:
- Model mix: 60% mix of opt-6b family (fast path), 40% llama-2.2-xxl family (slower, memory heavy)
- Effective throughput per A100-eq (with mixed quantization): ~140K tokens/sec for opt family, ~55K tokens/sec for llama-family
- Average tokens consumed per request (in+out): 2,020 tokens
- Effective concurrent decoding overhead: KV cache reuse reduces repeated context by ~8%

Sizing output:
- Steady GPU need to meet 1,100 reqs/s (current steady target): ~9.6 A100-eq -> round up to 10 GPUs
- To meet p95 < 400ms for short requests (<1k tokens), we recommend a split routing policy:
  * Short path (<=1k tokens): route to a 3-GPU low-latency shard with aggressive batching disabled (p95 modeled <350ms)
  * Long path (>1k tokens): route across the remaining 7 GPUs optimized for throughput (p95 ~600-700ms)
- This split reduces overall committed pool to 10 GPUs while giving Hyperion a stronger short-request p95 tail.

Operational notes & options to reduce commit:
- Quantize llama-family more aggressively (INT4 on non-critical ops) — could shave ~20% GPU need but requires validation for quality.
- Prefix/KV cache tuning: if Hyperion can increase cache hit rate to 20% (from current ~8%), GPUs drop to ~8.

Fallback & canary recommendation:
- Canary: 2-week bench + 30-day live canary on a mirrored subset of traffic (traffic steering at 5–10%)
- Emergency fallback: if overflow buffer exhausted, requests exceeding committed capacity should be automatically downgraded to a hosted Redwood-verified model with explicit customer opt-in for degraded latency/response quality. We can include a deterministic credit calculation: 1 credit = 0.5% monthly fee per 10-minute SLA breach window (example formula to be agreed).

I've uploaded detailed modeling to: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1HyperionModeling (see sheet 'Redwood_Model_Run_Aisha_May17').

Happy to present these findings on a quick call.

— Ben
Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Pricing sketch: committed pool + burst + SLA tiers — proposed path

Aisha — summarizing the path we recommend and the commercial ask so procurement has something concrete for legal: 

Proposed commercial summary (decision-for-signature draft):
- Committed pool: 10 A100-equivalent GPUs; 12-month term
- Burst: 30% additional GPU hours from Redwood shared capacity for transient surges (best-effort; documented windows)
- Routing: split short/long path as Ben recommended (3-GPU low-latency shard + 7-GPU throughput shard)
- SLA: Premium SLA for short-path requests (p95 < 400ms) with deterministic credits formula (1 credit = 0.5% monthly fee per 10-minute breach window; cumulative credit cap = 25% monthly fee)
- Discounts: 18% off list for 12-month paid monthly; up to 22% if 90% upfront payment (negotiable)
- Canary & rollback: 45-day MAP (14-day bench + 30-day live canary at 10% traffic); rollback triggers and responsible parties listed in attached term sheet draft.

Next steps:
1) Marissa team to produce a one-page term sheet and SLO appendix (by EOD May 19).
2) Hyperion to send procurement redlines (we have your doc) and confirm acceptance of the credit formula.
3) Schedule a technical run with Ben for validation and a 2-week bench slot.

If that looks right, I'll convert this into a term sheet and loop legal.

Thanks — looking forward to closing this out.

— Elliot
Head of Sales, Redwood Inference
